entries.description: Frames agent evaluations, benchmarks and leaderboards as held-constant ablations across three factors: Model, Harness, and Task Adaptation (none, pre-baked skill, or self-customization where the agent builds its own tools first). Use when deciding which eval cells to run next, designing a benchmark matrix, writing an eval report, or laying out a leaderboard UI so each product category gets a clear story without overwhelming viewers. Don't use for writing a single grader or task (build those first), or for generic statistics questions unrelated to agent evals.

Synchronizes all AAIF Working Group (wg-*) and foundation repositories, meeting minutes, charters, monthly reports, deliverables, reference architectures, and open pull requests from https://github.com/aaif/* into Google NotebookLM (https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/3f4ea1ea-fe19-4afe-8cbe-ac5f9950412d). Features full state-based lifecycle management (skip unchanged, update modified, add new, remove deleted/merged) with active credential validation, bi-weekly lookback synthesis, and automated public GitHub Gist reporting.

Triages the user's unread Chat, Email, and Calendar into an actionable "pay attention vs. ignore" digest. Uses a local user profile (~/.config/agent/user-profile.md) to personalize prioritization weights, key collaborators, and projects. If the profile is missing, the agent will guide the user to create one.

Orchestrates persona-based developer friction reviews on onboarding flows, recipes, tools, and CLIs. Spawns a persona subagent to follow documented steps from a cold start, records errors in a Friction Log artifact, and fixes verified issues across review loops. Use when testing developer experience (DX), walking a new developer journey, auditing README instructions, or validating recipes. Don't use for code review (use adlc-prosecutor or council), unit tests, or running agents in containers (use podman-agent-harness).

Synthesizes AI and developer ecosystem intelligence by combining Plushcap MCP (tech company engineering blogs, YouTube metrics, Hacker News activity, competitive spaces, and industry trend topics) with Good AI List (19,500+ open-source AI repositories, daily/weekly star velocity, developer activity, and category taxonomies). Use when asked to investigate AI tech trends, discover fast-growing open-source AI projects or breakout GitHub repositories, research tech company engineering momentum or blog activity, lookup items on goodailist.com or Plushcap, track developer metrics, analyze competitive spaces, or cross-reference enterprise tech announcements with open-source ecosystem adoption. Don't use for generic non-tech web search (use search_web) or single-file git operations (use vcs).

Capture Critical User Journey (CUJ) screenshots and GIFs from web apps using headless Chromium, keyed to the repo's feature map so each journey proves one named feature. Use when you need to verify UI changes through the real app, produce reviewable visual evidence for a PR, or document user flows. Don't use for component-level stories (use storybook).

Writes and tests Storybook stories for React components: one story per state, play functions, and batch screenshots. Use when asked for stories or component isolation. Don't use for building a whole UI feature (use ui-developer) or capturing app journeys (use cuj-screenshots).

End-to-end loop for building React/TypeScript UI features with agents - typed component, behavior tests, Storybook isolation, property tests for stateful UI, and feature-map-driven visual verification. Use when building or changing a UI feature or component, together with engineering-discipline. Don't use for a one-line style or copy tweak (core rules only), stories alone (use storybook), or journey capture alone (use cuj-screenshots).

Audits a whole repository and moves its rules down the trust order (structure, then verification, then prose) before agents write more code in it: lints with agent-actionable messages, directory boundaries, one blessed wrapper per nuance-heavy API, dead code and comment slop removed, a feature map, and a reusable verification driver. Use when preparing a repo for heavy agent use or an autonomous loop, when the same review finding or correction keeps coming back, or when asked to garden, de-slop, or harden a codebase. Don't use for a single feature or bug fix (use engineering-discipline), for slimming AGENTS.md alone (use checkup), or for reviewing one diff (use adlc-prosecutor).

Elixir and Phoenix coding standards: pattern matching, error tuples, OTP, Ecto, and LiveView conventions. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Elixir code, together with engineering-discipline for anything beyond a trivial edit. Don't use for non-Elixir backends or for repo-wide boundary rules (use codebase-gardening).

Core engineering loop for any code change bigger than a trivial edit. Picks a size tier, writes a short spec whose acceptance criteria each end in "Verify:" for medium work, debugs from root cause, never weakens tests or adds suppressions, and verifies through the real surface before claiming done. Use for a multi-file feature, a bug or ticket whose cause you still have to find, a refactor, or an unclear request, and load it together with any specialized skill (UI, Elixir, security). Don't use for a new project, a multi-PR build, or a risky migration (use spec-kit-adlc), or for repo-wide cleanup (use codebase-gardening).

Secure coding rules for web apps: input validation, output encoding, sessions, authentication, authorization, and secrets. Use when a change touches untrusted input, login, tokens, cookies, or access control, together with engineering-discipline. Don't use for auditing MCP server configs (use mcp-auditor) or for general code review.

Guide and best practices for creating, evaluating, and iteratively improving high-leverage skills for AI coding agents: when a skill is warranted, trigger descriptions, structure, and eval loops. Use when authoring or refining a SKILL.md outside CloudCode. Don't use in CloudCode (use skill-author) or for packaging skills into plugins (use skills-to-plugins).

Plans and de-risks a large build by pairing GitHub spec-kit (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md) with ADLC gates (spec-lint, premortem, rails-guard, prosecution) and, for parallel work, an agb fleet. Use when starting a new project or service, a feature that spans several PRs or weeks, or a risky migration or data, auth, or public-API change that is hard to revert. Don't use for a single-PR feature or a bug fix (use engineering-discipline), or for running one named ADLC gate on an existing spec (use adlc).

Create production-grade, synchronous terminal recordings (asciinema .cast) and interactive tabbed web walkthroughs for AI agents, developer tools, and CLI journeys. Includes PTY prompt-synchronization, intelligent time-compression, secret redaction, scenario banner structuring, and zoomable Mermaid flowchart companions.

Create branded architecture, IT current-state, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER/data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar/spider, loop/flywheel, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, Venn, pyramid/funnel, bar, line, Gantt and scatter charts, high-level, process, medallion, data flow, DP integration, or DP security matrix diagrams as standalone Material Design 3 HTML/SVG/PNG with subtle Google colors. Redraw .drawio/.drawio.png/.drawio.svg or Mermaid .mmd sources at a chosen size/detail; onboard brand tokens from a website; add semantic patterns, callouts, accessible motion, or sketchy/hand-drawn styling.

Create high-impact 1920x1080 (16:9) YouTube thumbnails and technical social hero cards from real UI screenshots using a programmatic Playwright HTML/CSS canvas. Preserves 100% lossless UI screenshot clarity while layering 3D perspective depth, percentage-locked feature spotlights, subtle dot-matrix textures, and multi-stop gradient typography.

Write, rewrite, or review technical prose (blog posts, articles, design docs, PR descriptions, system architectures, and social posts) in Alan Blount's authentic voice: the Pragmatic Builder. Combines 20+ years of software engineering experience with DevRel clarity, dry observational wit, subtle "muppet" warmth/enthusiasm, crisp analogies, and strict anti-AI discipline (no em-dashes, no buzzword fluff, no chatbot patterns). Use whenever asked to write in Alan's tone, sound like Alan, humanize text to his personal standards, or write developer-facing content for his projects.

Alan's standard workflow to produce a high-impact, viral X Article for the @GoogleCloudTech brand account from a trend, architecture pattern, repo, or launch: connect the trend to Google Cloud Gemini platform + live developer context, propose title/hook angles first, draft to the proven structure in Alan's Pragmatic Builder voice (20-year dev experience, muted "muppet" warmth, dry technical wit, parenthetical asides, zero em-dashes, and strict anti-AI discipline), generate clean Engineering Graph Paper diagrams, and publish to a Google Doc on approval. Use whenever Alan wants to draft an X Article, turn a trend/spec/repo into an article, or brainstorm @GoogleCloudTech content angles.

Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads naturally without changing what it says. Use when editing or reviewing prose for inflated claims, sales language, vague sources, repetitive structure, stock AI words, passive voice, filler, or chatbot artifacts. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing." Don't use for writing new text in Alan's voice (use alan-writing-style or alanblount_voice).
